items.title: How cruise control and book-and-claim can decarbonize US railroads
items.summary: Shifting freight from road to rail could avoid the release of millions of tons of carbon dioxide and help companies cut shipping emissions.

items.title: This new framework measures corporate chemical footprints
items.summary: The Safer Chemistry Impact Fund (SCI Fund), an initiative backed by Google and Apple, has released a framework that companies can tap to measure chemicals used in their products and supply chains, flag potential hazards and track progress in addressing them.

items.title: Scotland’s AI Growth Zone secures £300m investment
items.summary: The Government has earmarked £300m to invest in an AI Growth Zone in Lanarkshire, with new research suggesting that more developers are targeting greenbelts to build data centre infrastructure.

items.title: Welsh Government announces new net-zero by 2040 target
items.summary: As part of the proposed Climate and Nature Action Plan, Wales is aiming to be net-zero by 2040, 10 years ahead of the rest of the UK.

items.title: Unlocking the value of bio-based materials in the built environment
items.summary: Increasing the availability and adoption of bio-based materials at scale brings both significant opportunities and complex challenges.

items.title: Green groups debunk Tory claims that ditching net-zero would cut energy bills
items.summary: At the launch of a new report from Conservative-aligned think tank Onward, Shadow Energy Security Claire Coutinho raised questions over the cost of clean power.

items.title: Schott drops ‘climate-neutral’ production goal in favour of SBTi targets
items.summary: The glass manufacturer has announced that it is abandoning its offset-reliant, climate-neutral goal for 2030, focusing instead on newly validated science-based targets.

items.title: New Zealand curbs climate harm lawsuits against companies
items.summary: The New Zealand Government has passed controversial legislation to prevent lawsuits from being carried out that hold companies liable for damage due to climate change.

items.title: US Government wants business exemptions from ‘onerous’ EU CSRD and CSDDD
items.summary: The US Government has called on the European Union to revisit changes to both the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) and the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), stating that it places ‘costly and onerous’ obligations on US businesses aiming to sell into Europe.

items.title: FOUR WEEKS to go until edie’s Sustainable Supply Chains Summit
items.summary: Join us on 17 September for a unique opportunity to gain expert-led insights through thought leadership and industry panels featuring top professionals in sustainability, supply chain and procurement.
